findings.evidence:
Two columns, `birthday` (month and day, no year) and `phone`, are added to `profiles`, filled only for members who opt in. They are
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the purpose, not to the profile (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). Add a requirement and a scenario to specs/birthday-greetings/spec.md: when a member opts out, `birthday` and `phone` are cleared on their profile. Today the spec only covers opting in, so a member who withdraws keeps both fields stored for the life of the profile with no purpose left. Add the matching task in tasks.md.
findings.title: Opting out does not erase the birthday and phone number

findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: State how long the nightly backups holding `birthday` and `phone` are kept and how an erasure (opt-out or account deletion) reaches them — for instance a bounded backup rotation after which erased values are gone, documented in the design (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). As written, a member's birthday and phone number erased from `profiles` survive in every backup with no stated expiry.
findings.title: No retention or purge rule for the copies in nightly backups

findings.evidence:
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: record Textly as a processor (Art. 28 contract) and the Chapter V mechanism for the transfer to the United States (adequacy decision / Data Privacy Framework certification or standard contractual clauses), and add Textly to the records of processing (Art. 30). Also confirm the display name is needed in the message; if the text can be generic, send the phone number only.
findings.title: Transfer of phone numbers and names to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: state the purpose and lawful basis of the processing (presumably consent given by the opt-in, Art. 6(1)(a) and Art. 7) and whether these texts count as direct marketing under the ePrivacy Directive; if so, the opt-in wording must say so and withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent (see R-privacy-1).
findings.title: Lawful basis for marketing text messages not stated
